note: Format-1 conformance vectors generated by conformance/v1/generate.mjs with the TypeScript core as the executable reference. A conforming implementation reproduces every `expect` from the corresponding `input` (histories under conformance/v1/histories). Regeneration is deterministic: `node conformance/v1/generate.mjs --check` reproduces these files byte for byte.

nextKey.note: the next key the genesis commitments name (test key only); rotation-v1 has no commitment

vectors.purpose: A format-1 handover history with owner-signed control events, a simulated admission, a receipt, an obligation and a succession replays to a stable head.
Every prefix of a valid format-1 history is valid: the history as it stood before the succession.
A control event without its owner signature is refused (CONTROL_AUTHORIZATION_INVALID).
A control event whose signature bytes were altered is refused (CONTROL_AUTHORIZATION_INVALID).
Two independently valid, signed grants swapped in position are refused (CONTROL_AUTHORIZATION_INVALID): each signature binds the head before its event.
Editing the content of a signed grant (its expiry) invalidates the owner signature over its effect hash (CONTROL_AUTHORIZATION_INVALID).
A control event claiming a key id the genesis does not declare is refused (CONTROL_AUTHORIZATION_INVALID).
The genesis commits the owner keys to the digest of their next key (nextKeyDigests, part of the history id; pre-rotation from the first event); createLocalOwner writes it by default.
A genesis whose next-key commitment names one of its own owner keys is refused (EVENT_DATA_INVALID): a declared key can never be revealed as a next key.
A genesis whose next-key commitment repeats a digest is refused by the closed schema (EVENT_DATA_INVALID).
A genesis whose next-key commitment is empty is refused by the closed schema (EVENT_DATA_INVALID): a genesis without a commitment leaves nextKeyDigests out.

On a history created without a next-key commitment, OWNER_KEYS_ROTATED signed by the current owner key replaces the owner key set: the control events after it are signed by the new key and the history replays.
After a rotation the retired owner key can no longer sign a control event (CONTROL_AUTHORIZATION_INVALID), although it signed every control event before the rotation.
A rotation signed by a key the history never declared is refused (CONTROL_AUTHORIZATION_INVALID): only a key in force may replace the owner keys.
A rotation that brings a retired key id back is refused (TRANSITION_INVALID), even when signed by the key in force: a retired key never returns.
A rotation that keeps a key id but binds it to a different public key is refused (TRANSITION_INVALID).
A legacy (continuity-event/0.2) history has no owner keys: OWNER_KEYS_ROTATED is UNSUPPORTED_EVENT_TYPE there.
An owner key epoch without a commitment rotates freely, signed by the current key alone, and may start a commitment for the new set (nextKeyDigests).

An owner key epoch without a commitment gets one by a rotation that keeps every owner key and carries nextKeyDigests (the commitment-only rotation that owner commit-next-key records); the same key keeps signing.
A rotation that keeps every owner key and carries no nextKeyDigests changes nothing and is refused (TRANSITION_INVALID).

A rotation out of a committed epoch that reveals the committed key, carries that key's signature over the event's control-authorization challenge (nextKeyAuthorizations) and commits the new set to its own next key is accepted; the revealed key signs from the next position on.

A rotation out of a committed epoch to a key the commitment does not name is refused (TRANSITION_INVALID), although the current key signed it and the new key proved possession: the current key alone cannot rotate.
Revealing the committed public key without a signature by it (no nextKeyAuthorizations) is refused (TRANSITION_INVALID): the public key alone proves nothing.
A rotation out of a committed epoch that reveals and proves the committed key but carries no nextKeyDigests is refused (TRANSITION_INVALID): the commitment chain must continue.

A rotation that keeps every owner key and commits to another next key, out of an epoch that already has a commitment, is refused (TRANSITION_INVALID), although the key in force signed it: it reveals no committed key, so a leaked current key cannot replace the commitment.
An ANCHOR_RECORDED event whose anchored head is a prefix of this history is accepted.
A correctly signed anchor whose anchored head hash is not a prefix hash of this history is refused (TRANSITION_INVALID).

Owner-signed WITNESSES_BOUND (two remote witnesses, the first with its signed REGISTERED receipt of this genesis, and the policy minimum) then WITNESSES_UNBOUND (the second) replay; the history binds the first witness under the newest policy. A verifier that does not speak the witness protocol still reports the bindings.
A binding whose witness list was edited after signing is refused: the owner signature covers every witness (CONTROL_AUTHORIZATION_INVALID).
A binding whose registration is not a witness receipt (here: a receipt record with its inclusion proof removed) is refused, although the owner signed it (TRANSITION_INVALID).
A binding that files witness A's receipt under witness B's verifier key is refused: a registration must be signed by the witness it binds (TRANSITION_INVALID).
A binding whose registration is witness A's valid receipt of this history plus a field a witness receipt does not have is refused: the receipt record is closed (TRANSITION_INVALID).
A binding whose registration is witness A's valid receipt of another history's REGISTERED leaf is refused: it must name this genesis (TRANSITION_INVALID).
A binding whose policy minimum has quorum 0 is refused by the closed schema (EVENT_DATA_INVALID).
A binding without its policy minimum is refused by the closed schema (EVENT_DATA_INVALID): every binding event states the policy in force after it.
A binding whose policy quorum (2) exceeds the witnesses bound after it (1) is refused (TRANSITION_INVALID).
A binding whose witness URL carries a query string is refused by the closed schema (EVENT_DATA_INVALID): a witness URL is http(s)://host[/path] without userinfo, query, fragment or trailing slash.
A binding that names one verifier key twice is refused by the closed schema (EVENT_DATA_INVALID).
A binding of sixteen more witnesses on a history that already binds one (seventeen bound after it) is refused (TRANSITION_INVALID): at most sixteen remote witnesses are bound.
A legacy (continuity-event/0.2) history has no owner keys and binds no witness: WITNESSES_BOUND is UNSUPPORTED_EVENT_TYPE there.

Binding a witness the history already binds (the same verifier key) re-binds it in place: its URL, name and registration are replaced and it is still bound once (how a witness bound while unreachable gets its REGISTERED receipt later).
An unbinding that names a witness the history does not bind is refused (TRANSITION_INVALID).
An unbinding that records an accepted loss of a head this history contains is refused: nothing was lost (TRANSITION_INVALID).
An unbinding whose accepted loss names a witness the event does not unbind (here: the one that stays bound) is refused (TRANSITION_INVALID): a loss is accepted only for a witness being unbound.
An unbinding that records an accepted loss (the owner's reason and a head the witness holds that this copy lacks) is accepted; the witness is no longer bound.

An owner-signed ANCHOR_RECORDED (anchor "custom") whose receipt is shaped like an unbinding of the bound witness is accepted as an anchor and changes nothing: the history still binds the witness under the signed policy.
On a history that binds no witness, an ANCHOR_RECORDED whose receipt is shaped like a binding of witness A binds nothing (no bound witnesses, no policy).
ANCHOR_RECORDED.data.anchor names one of the anchor kinds local-head-file, rekor-v2 or custom: an anchor naming another ("http-witness") is refused by the closed schema (EVENT_DATA_INVALID).

A format-1 history migrated from the legacy handover fixture (26 events re-recorded verbatim under owner signatures, runtime signatures verified against the legacy shadow heads) replays; its genesis commits the new owner key to a next key.
Dropping a re-recorded event inside the migrated prefix breaks the legacy shadow heads the runtime-signed admission binds; the replay is refused inside the prefix (TRANSITION_INVALID).

A migrated history cut off before the end of its declared prefix (head position below migratedFrom.position) is refused once the replay completes: TRANSITION_INVALID, migrated prefix incomplete. Every event present is valid on its own, so only the completed-replay check catches it.

A genesis that claims a shorter migrated prefix than the one re-recorded is refused (TRANSITION_INVALID), even with every owner signature redone over it: the legacy shadow hash at the claimed end is not the source head.

An owner-signed ed25519 runtime session admission inside a migrated legacy prefix is refused (EVENT_DATA_INVALID): the prefix re-records legacy events, whose session credentials are Ethereum addresses.
An owner-signed WITNESSES_BOUND inside a migrated legacy prefix is refused (TRANSITION_INVALID): the prefix re-records legacy events, and a witness binding is not one.
The successor may do what it was separately granted.
The successor holds the duty and must NOT inherit the power that created it.
A terminated agent is refused before any authority is considered (AGENT_INACTIVE).
An expected head that is not the replayed head yields INDETERMINATE HISTORY_RELATION_UNVERIFIED.
An evaluation time before the head is not causal (CAUSAL_TIME_INVALID).
A request under a different deployment is refused (DOMAIN_MISMATCH).
A delegated grant that requires an intersection partner held by the actor is allowed; the proof controls the delegation chain and the partner.
A plain delegation from the lead to the analyst is allowed.
A grant whose required intersection partner is not held by the actor fails MISSING_INTERSECTION.
A ROOT prohibition on the root grant blocks the lead's otherwise valid payment from the vault.
A GLOBAL prohibition by the policy source blocks an action any grant would allow.
A revoked grant fails REVOKED.
A grant whose expiry passed fails EXPIRED.
A grant whose notBefore lies ahead fails NOT_YET_VALID.
A quantitative grant needs an amount in the request (AMOUNT_REQUIRED).
An amount above the per-request ceiling fails AMOUNT_EXCEEDED.
An amount at the ceiling is allowed.
Two admissions consumed 90 of a 100 cumulative budget; 20 more fails CUMULATIVE_AMOUNT_EXCEEDED.
The remaining 10 of the cumulative budget is still allowed after two admissions.
One admission exhausted a single-transaction grant (TRANSACTION_COUNT_EXCEEDED).
A terminated agent is refused (AGENT_INACTIVE) even though its grant is live.
An active agent holding no grant at all fails NO_AUTHORITY.
The designated successor gains nothing from the succession rule before the transfer: the leaver's grant does not follow.
Decisions on the migrated history match the legacy fixture: the successor may do what it was separately granted.
Decisions on the migrated history match the legacy fixture: the successor does not inherit the collection power.
The terminated predecessor keeps the duty visible; its assignment moved to the successor; its grant was revoked.
The successor holds the tenure and the assignment and keeps its own grants.
Before the succession the predecessor is active, holds the tenure and owns the open duty.
An agent the history never created is ABSENT.
SURVIVES on the migrated history matches the legacy fixture for the terminated predecessor.
An attestation of a head before the rotation, signed by the key that was in force then, still verifies after that key was retired.
The head that ends with the rotation belongs to the old key set: the retired key's attestation of it verifies.
The new key governs only from the position after the rotation: its attestation of the rotation head itself does not verify.
An attestation of a head after the rotation signed by the retired key does not verify.
An attestation of a head after the rotation signed by the new key verifies.
A correctly signed attestation of a head this history does not contain is not an attestation of this history (prefix false).
